newsitem.title: SPAIN: Peseta brushes aside Sweden's EMU decision.
newsitem.headline: Peseta brushes aside Sweden's EMU decision.

text.p: The peseta remained largely unruffled by Sweden's decision to skip the launch of Europe's single currency and Germany's deal on its gold revaluation, traders said.
Traders said the focus had shifted back to France and the market was now keenly awaiting clar policy from new Socialist Prime Minister Lionel Jospin on the euro.
"In the market there is a degree of fear that France may adopt measures that would signify a delay for EMU," said one dealer.
But in any event the peseta will likely remain locked in its 84.00 to 85.00 per mark band for the near future, traders said.
By 1630 GMT, the peseta stood at 84.45/48 against the mark compared with levels seen late on Monday of 84.47/49.
Swedish Prime Minister Goran Persson said his country would not join Europe's economic and monetary union at the proposed start in January 1999.

In Germany, the Bundesbank and Finance Ministry struck a deal over gold revaluation under which gold and currency reserves will be revalued at the end of 1997, but the profits only transferred in 1998.
